messages:
Alina: Quick log: onboarding Zephyrus-lite (hf -> redwood) for int8. Ran the standard summarization suite and saw a systematic bump localized to comma/period tokens and mid-heads. Seems similar to past qkv interleave issues but with a rotary twist.
Alina: Convert cmd: `python tools/convert_hf.py --model Zephyrus/zephyrus-lite --out redwood/zephyrus-lite --quant int8`
Marta: Did you try dumping per-head weight correlations vs the upstream fp16? A low per-head cosine usually screams reorder.
Alina: Yup — per_head_cosine: median 0.98 but heads 9..14 drop to 0.4-0.6. Also ran token-id delta sweep and saw punctuation ids have larger logit deltas.
Rafael: Two possibilities: (1) qkv split ordering wrong (interleaved vs chunked), (2) rotary freq/scale mismatch that disproportionately affects tokens with short contexts (punctuation often short preceding context). Which converter version?
Alina: converter 0.9.1. It auto-splits fused qkv -> 3 shards by contiguous slicing. HF checkpoint actually documents `qkv` interleaved in their config note. Converter didn't catch that.
Jamie: Could also be tokenizer bit: HF vocab uses soft-unicode normalizer (NFKC) while our tokenizer pipeline used NFC in pipeline by mistake last week — subtle id shifts can amplify in quant. Did you compare vocab hash + id map?
Priya: I'll run a 100k token sweep to verify shadow ids. Also will throw in the `emoji` heavy set — we saw previously that surrogate pairs expose endian/tokenization edge cases.
Alina: I patched converter to support `--qkv-split=interleaved` (reorders slices by head). Re-ran int8 bench: ppl delta vs fp16 reduced from +9.1% to +1.5%. So ordering was most of it.
Rafael: Nice find. But the residual +1.5% could be rotary. Mistral-derived blocks sometimes use per-head rotary scale (headwise alpha) which our runtime currently normalizes globally. Quantization amplifies small amplitude mismatches.
Marta: Suggestion: add a tiny unit test in convert CI that (a) tries both split modes and picks the one with higher median per-head cosine against fp16, (b) runs a micro-rotary drift check: feed a repeated token pattern and compute phase drift per head across positions. If drift > epsilon, warn.
Jamie: Agree. Also add a tokenizer id parity test: map HF ids -> runtime ids for first 2000 tokens and compute edit distance; if >0 fail conversion. That will catch NFC/NFKC mismatches early.
Priya: Running tokenizer sweep now. Early results: 0.02% id differences concentrated on ligatures and whitespace variants. I'll push a small normalizer shim in preprocessing to enforce NFKC before tokenization for new conversions.
Alina: For the converter UX: I'll add `--detect-qkv-order` that tries both reorderings and selects best by per-head cosine with fp16 sample. Also will emit metadata: `qkv_order: interleaved|chunked` in the converted manifest.
Rafael: On the runtime side, I propose making KV cache agnostic: store cache with explicit head ordering tag and provide a shim at load that permutes cache to expected layout. That avoids cross-version warm-start breakages during rollouts.
Marta: Add test where you warm-start a quant model from a fp16 cache and check next-token logits for bitwise-equality within tolerance after permute. We'll catch incompatibilities early.
build-bot: CI started: `eng-ml/zephyrus-lite-convert` (matrix: split-detect, rotary-check, tokenizer-sweep) -> https://ci.redwood/internal/12789
Alina: CI quick pass: split-detect picked `interleaved` for Zephyrus-lite. Rotary-check flagged small headwise scaling differences; added note in artifact. Tokenizer-sweep found the NFKC diffs Priya mentioned.
Jamie: Action items: Alina -> PR for detect-qkv-order + manifest field + update README. Priya -> normalizer shim PR + tokenizer id parity test. Rafael -> runtime KV-order tag + permute shim + warm-start microbench. Marta -> add rotary drift unit test and include in conversion CI.
Alina: I'll also bake a small `convert-smoke` artifact that contains per-head cosine CSV, rotary-phase plots, and token id diff list for each conversion. That'll be helpful for future triage.
Priya: Adding note to model onboarding doc: "Always run `convert --detect-qkv-order` and check tokenizer parity before creating a canary".
build-bot: CI complete: all matrix jobs succeeded, 1 advisory (rotary head variance) -> https://ci.redwood/internal/12789/artifacts
Jamie: Great work. Let's run a gated canary on Dedicated tomorrow and keep an eye on chat-summarize SLOs. If anyone hits similar PPL bumps, follow the checklist above and tag `eng-ml`.
